## 020 — International Standard Book Number \(ISBN\)

Records the ISBN uniquely identifying the specific edition/format of the item\.

*Source: AACR2 1\.8B1  |  ISBD Area 8  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 020*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

020

$a

ISBN

Enter the 13\-digit ISBN with no spaces or hyphens, exactly as printed \(usually on the back cover or verso of the title page\)\.

9780521866446

020

$c

Terms of availability

Price or availability statement, if recorded by local policy\.

₹495\.00

Required vs\. optional: $a is required whenever an ISBN is printed on the item; $c is optional per local policy\.

### ISBD punctuation for this field

- No prescribed leading mark within the field itself; ISBN is its own Area 8 statement, introduced by '\. — ' if run on after Area 7 notes\.

### Exceptions and special cases

- If the item shows a 10\-digit ISBN only, convert to the current 13\-digit form for entry \(per ISBN Agency conversion rules\), and may add the invalid 10\-digit form in a note if needed\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Typing hyphens or spaces into $a\.
- Entering the ISBN of a different edition than the one in hand\.

__Full field example: __*9780521866446*

## 082 — Dewey Decimal Classification Number

Provides the call number used for shelving and subject grouping, built from DDC class number \+ Cutter mark\.

*Source: AACR2 — \(classification, not AACR2 descriptive rule\)  |  ISBD — \(outside ISBD areas\)  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 082*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

082

$a

Classification number

DDC class number \(Call No\.\) assigned from the schedules/WebDewey for the work's primary subject\.

323

082

$b

Item number \(Cutter mark\)

First three CAPITAL letters of the author's/editor's/compiler's surname\.

GEA

082

$2

Edition number

DDC edition used to assign the number \(e\.g\. 23rd\)\.

23

Required vs\. optional: $a and $b required for every item; $2 required to record which DDC edition was used\.

### Exceptions and special cases

- For works with a personal main entry, Cutter from the AUTHOR's surname; for works entered under title, Cutter from the first word of the title \(excluding articles\)\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Using more or fewer than three letters in the Cutter mark\.
- Leaving $2 blank so future re\-classification cannot verify which DDC edition was applied\.

__Full field example: __*323 GEA \(22nd DDC ed\.\)*

## 100 — Main Entry — Personal Name

The principal access point when one person is chiefly responsible for the intellectual content of the work\.

*Source: AACR2 21\.1A \(choice of personal main entry\); 22\.1–22\.19 \(form of personal name heading\)  |  ISBD — \(main entry is an AACR2/MARC access\-point concept, not an ISBD area\)  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 100*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

100

$a

Personal name

Surname, First name — comma between surname and forename; no full stop after the name\.

Gearty, Conor

100

$b

Numeration

Roman/Arabic numeral following a name \(royalty, popes\)\.

III

100

$c

Titles and other words with name

Added only if needed to distinguish the person, or the person is not known by a forename\.

Dr\.

100

$d

Dates

Birth–death years joined by a hyphen; a living author is given as birth year plus hyphen\.

1875\-1926

100

$q

Fuller form of name

Expansion of an initialised forename, given in parentheses\.

\(Rainer Maria\)

100

$e

Relator term

Role: author, editor, compiler, etc\.

author

Required vs\. optional: $a is required; $d/$c/$q are added only when needed to identify/distinguish the person \(AACR2 22\.17–22\.19\)\.

### ISBD punctuation for this field

- No terminal punctuation after the name itself; $d dates are enclosed by nothing \(plain hyphenated string\) and follow $a directly\.

### Exceptions and special cases

- If two authors of equal responsibility exist, only the FIRST\-named becomes the 100 main entry; the second becomes a 700 added entry \(AACR2 21\.6B\)\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Adding a full stop after the surname/forename in $a\.
- Inverting a corporate name into $a by mistake — 100 is for PERSONS only\.

__Full field example: __*100  1\#  $a Gearty, Conor\.*

## 110 — Main Entry — Corporate Body

Principal access point when a work satisfies AACR2's specific corporate\-responsibility test \(not merely 'published by' a body\)\.

*Source: AACR2 21\.1B1, 21\.1B2 \(categories of works entered under corporate body\)  |  ISBD —  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 110*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

110

$a

Corporate/jurisdiction name

Natural word order, no inversion, no comma — used ONLY when the 21\.1B test is met\.

World Health Organization

110

$b

Subordinate unit

Department/division entered after the parent body\.

Library Division

110

$e

Relator term

issuing body, compiler, etc\.

issuing body

Required vs\. optional: $a required; $b only if the item is issued in the name of a subordinate unit\.

### Exceptions and special cases

- AACR2 21\.1B2 limits corporate main entry to: \(a\) works of administrative nature about the body itself; \(b\) legal/governmental/religious works of that class; \(c\) works recording the collective thought of the body; \(d\) works reporting collective activity of a conference/expedition/event; \(e\) sound recordings/films/broadcasts where the body is the performer; \(f\) certain cartographic works\. All other corporate involvement is an ADDED entry \(710\), with the work entered under title or personal author instead\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Entering under corporate body simply because the body published/sponsored the work — publication alone never justifies a 110 main entry \(AACR2 21\.1B3 explicitly excludes this\)\.

__Full field example: __*110  2\#  $a World Health Organization\.*

## 111 — Main Entry — Meeting/Conference

Principal access point when the published item is the proceedings/report of a named meeting, and the meeting itself \(not an individual editor\) is treated as corporately responsible\.

*Source: AACR2 21\.1B2\(d\)  |  ISBD —  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 111*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

111

$a

Meeting name

Natural word order, no comma\.

International Conference on Human Rights

111

$d

Date of meeting

Numeric year/date\.

2024

111

$c

Location of meeting

City name, no brackets\.

Bangalore

Required vs\. optional: $a required; $d and $c required whenever known, to disambiguate recurring conference series\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Using 111 for a book merely ABOUT a conference \(that is a 610/650 subject entry, not a 111 main/added entry\)\.

__Full field example: __*111  2\#  $a International Conference on Human Rights $d \(2024 : $c Bangalore\)*

## 245 — Title Statement

Records the title proper, any subtitle, and the statement of responsibility exactly as they appear on the chief source of information \(title page for a printed book\)\.

*Source: AACR2 1\.1 \(title and statement of responsibility area, all sub\-rules\)  |  ISBD Area 1  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 245*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

245

$a

Title proper

Transcribe exactly as on the title page; ends with ' :' if a subtitle follows, or with '\.' if nothing follows\.

Can human rights survive :

245

$b

Other title information \(subtitle\)

Transcribe subtitle; ends with ' /' before the statement of responsibility\.

a short story /

245

$c

Statement of responsibility

See Section 3 for full scenario\-by\-scenario rules\.

by Conor Gearty\.

245

$h

General Material Designation \(GMD\)

Enclosed in square brackets after title proper, if local policy uses GMDs\.

\[electronic resource\]

Required vs\. optional: $a is mandatory in every record; $b only if a subtitle is present on the source; $c whenever a statement of responsibility appears\.

### ISBD punctuation for this field

- $a ends with ' :' only if $b follows; otherwise ends the whole field with a full stop if $c is absent\.
- $b always ends with ' /' before $c\.
- See Section 3 for all $c punctuation rules\.

### Exceptions and special cases

- Take the title from the TITLE PAGE, never the cover, spine, or a running head, even if worded differently \(AACR2 1\.0A, 1\.1B1\)\.
- If the title page has no title at all, supply one in square brackets from the rest of the item or a reference source, per AACR2 1\.1B7\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Taking the title/subtitle wording from the front cover instead of the title page\.
- Placing the statement of responsibility inside $a or $b instead of its own $c\.

__Full field example: __*245  1\#  $a Can human rights survive : $b a short story / $c by Conor Gearty\.*

## 250 — Edition Statement

Records the edition of the item in hand, when the title page indicates it is not the first edition, or otherwise differs textually from other editions\.

*Source: AACR2 1\.2 \(edition area\)  |  ISBD Area 2  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 250*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

250

$a

Edition statement

Copy as printed, abbreviated per AACR2 \(e\.g\. 'ed\.' for edition, 'rev\.' for revised\)\.

12th ed\.

250

$b

Statement of responsibility relating to edition

Named only if a person/body is responsible for THIS edition specifically \(e\.g\. a reviser\), introduced by '/'\.

/ revised by J\. Smith

Required vs\. optional: $a is given only when an edition statement appears on the source; omitted entirely for a first/only edition with no such statement\.

### ISBD punctuation for this field

- Field is introduced by '\. — ' if run on from the previous area; ends with a full stop unless $b \(with its own '/'\) follows\.

### Exceptions and special cases

- Numbers are converted to the standard abbreviation form set out in AACR2 Appendix B \(e\.g\. '2nd ed\.', not 'Second Edition'\)\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Recording 'Reprinted 2015' as an edition statement — a reprint with no textual change is a 500 note, not a 250 edition statement \(AACR2 1\.2 note\)\.

__Full field example: __*250  \#\#  $a 12th ed\.*

## 260 — Publication, Distribution, etc\.

Records where, by whom, and when the item was published\.

*Source: AACR2 1\.4 \(publication, distribution area\)  |  ISBD Area 4  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 260*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

260

$a

Place of publication

City as printed; if 2\+ places given, record only the first, ending with ' :'\.

Cambridge :

260

$b

Name of publisher

As printed, ending with ','\.

Cambridge University Press,

260

$c

Date of publication

Copyright/publication year, ending with '\.'

2006\.

Required vs\. optional: All three subfields required whenever available; if place/publisher is unknown, supply '\[S\.l\.\]' / '\[s\.n\.\]' per AACR2 1\.4C6/1\.4D6\.

### ISBD punctuation for this field

- $a ends ' :' before $b; $b ends ',' before $c; $c ends '\.' \(full stop\) closing Area 4\.

### Exceptions and special cases

- If the copyright date differs from the actual publication/printing date, and no publication date is available, use the copyright date preceded by 'c' \(e\.g\. 'c2006'\) per AACR2 1\.4F6\.
- A probable date not printed on the item is enclosed in brackets with a question mark: '\[2006?\]'\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Recording every place of publication listed on the title page instead of only the first\.
- Omitting the comma after the publisher's name\.

__Full field example: __*260  \#\#  $a Cambridge : $b Cambridge University Press, $c 2006\.*

## 300 — Physical Description

Describes the physical form of the item: extent, illustrative content, dimensions, and any accompanying material\.

*Source: AACR2 1\.5 \(physical description area\)  |  ISBD Area 5  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 300*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

300

$a

Extent

Roman\-numeral prelim pages \+ Arabic total pages, abbreviated 'p\.'

xvi, 174 p\.

300

$b

Other physical details

Illustration statement \(e\.g\. 'ill\.', 'col\. ill\.'\)\.

ill\.

300

$c

Dimensions

Height of the volume in centimetres\.

24 cm

300

$e

Accompanying material

Introduced by 'With', for CDs/maps/DVDs issued with the item\.

With 1 CD

Required vs\. optional: $a is always required; $b, $c, $e recorded when applicable\.

### ISBD punctuation for this field

- $a is followed by ' :' if $b \(illustration statement\) is present; $b is followed by ' ;' before $c \(dimensions\); $e is introduced by ' \+ ' at the very end\.

### Exceptions and special cases

- For a multi\-volume set, extent is given as the number of physical volumes \(e\.g\. '3 v\.'\) rather than a page count\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Recording total pages only, omitting Roman\-numeral preliminary pages\.
- Placing the accompanying\-material note in a 500 field instead of 300$e when it is a physical description matter\.

__Full field example: __*300  \#\#  $a xvi, 174 p\. : $b ill\. ; $c 24 cm\.*

## 500 — General Note

Records any general information about the item not accommodated in a more specific note field\.

*Source: AACR2 1\.7A \(notes, general rule\)  |  ISBD Area 7  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 500*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

500

$a

General note

Free\-text note in full\-sentence form, ending with a full stop\.

Includes index\.

Required vs\. optional: Optional — used whenever information helps identification or use of the item\.

### ISBD punctuation for this field

- Each note is its own independent sentence; no ISBD mark links separate note fields to each other\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Cramming multiple unrelated notes into a single 500 field instead of repeating the field\.

__Full field example: __*500  \#\#  $a "Originally published in French in 1985"\-\-Title page verso\.*

## 504 — Bibliography, etc\. Note

States that the work includes a bibliography, discography, filmography, and/or index\.

*Source: AACR2 1\.7B18  |  ISBD Area 7  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 504*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

504

$a

Bibliography note

'Includes bibliography' \+ page range, and 'and index' if applicable\.

Includes bibliography \(p\.158\-169\) and index\.

Required vs\. optional: Given whenever the item includes a formal bibliography/index\.

__Full field example: __*504  \#\#  $a Includes bibliographical references \(p\. 158\-169\) and index\.*

## 520 — Summary, Abstract, Annotation

Provides a brief, objective summary of the work's content/scope, useful in OPAC display\.

*Source: AACR2 — \(a MARC/library\-practice note, not a numbered AACR2 rule\)  |  ISBD Area 7  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 520*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

520

$a

Summary note

Concise, neutral description of scope/content\.

Examines the compatibility of human rights with counter\-terrorism law\.

520

$u

URI

Link to a fuller summary/blurb online, if available\.

https://example\.com/summary

Required vs\. optional: Optional; recommended for non\-fiction and reference works\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Copying publisher's promotional blurb verbatim instead of a neutral summary\.

## 586 — Awards Note

Records any literary/academic award the work has received\.

*Source: AACR2 1\.7B \(general note provision, applied to awards\)  |  ISBD Area 7  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 586*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

586

$a

Awards note

Name of the award and year\.

Pulitzer Prize, 2011\.

Required vs\. optional: Given only when the item states it received an award\.

__Full field example: __*586  \#\#  $a Booker Prize, 2012\.*

## 600 — Subject Added Entry — Personal Name

Provides subject access when the work is ABOUT a person \(biography, criticism of an author's work, etc\.\)\.

*Source: AACR2 21 \(choice/form is per name\-authority rules\); subject heading assignment itself follows LCSH/Sears, not AACR2  |  ISBD —  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 600*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

600

$a

Personal name \(as subject\)

Surname, First name of the person the work is ABOUT\.

Gandhi, Mahatma

600

$d

Dates

Birth–death years, hyphenated\.

1869\-1948

600

$x

General subdivision

Topical subdivision under the name, linked by ' — '\.

Political career

600

$v

Form subdivision

Form/genre of material, e\.g\. Biography\.

Biography

Required vs\. optional: $a required; subdivisions \($x/$y/$z/$v\) added as needed following the subject\-heading list in use\.

### ISBD punctuation for this field

- Each subdivision is linked to the previous element by ' — ' \(space\-dash\-space\), per LC Subject Headings Manual, not an ISBD mark\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Using 600 for the AUTHOR of the work \(that is 100\), rather than the SUBJECT of the work \(600\) — a common confusion when a book is both by and about the same person \(e\.g\. an autobiography needs both a 100 and a 600 for that person\)\.

## 610 — Subject Added Entry — Corporate Name

Provides subject access when the work is ABOUT an organisation, institution, or corporate body\.

*Source: AACR2 — \(subject cataloguing practice, LCSH/Sears\)  |  ISBD —  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 610*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

610

$a

Corporate name \(as subject\)

Natural word order, no comma\.

United Nations

610

$x

General subdivision

Topical subdivision\.

History

Required vs\. optional: $a required\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Confusing 610 \(subject\) with 710 \(added entry for a contributor/publisher body\) — 610 is used only when the body IS the topic\.

## 650 — Subject Added Entry — Topical Term

Provides the main topical subject access points for retrieval\.

*Source: AACR2 — \(subject cataloguing practice, LCSH/Sears\)  |  ISBD —  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 650*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

650

$a

Topical term

Main subject keyword/phrase; no terminal punctuation\.

Human rights

650

$z

Geographic subdivision

Country/place subdivision\.

India

650

$y

Chronological subdivision

Time period\.

21st century

650

$2

Source of heading

Controlled vocabulary used \(lcsh, sears, etc\.\)\.

lcsh

Required vs\. optional: $a required for every subject entry; subdivisions and $2 added per local subject\-heading policy\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Inventing free\-text subject terms instead of using an authorised list \(LCSH/Sears/local thesaurus\)\.

## 700 — Added Entry — Personal Name

Gives an access point for every person associated with the work who is not the 100 main entry — co\-authors, editors, translators, illustrators, compilers named in 245$c\.

*Source: AACR2 21\.6 \(shared responsibility\), 21\.30B \(added entries for collaborators\)  |  ISBD —  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 700*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

700

$a

Personal name

Surname, First name — normalised heading form, independent of the exact wording used in 245$c\.

Rabassa, Gregory

700

$e

Relator term

translator, editor, illustrator, compiler, etc\.

translator

Required vs\. optional: One 700 for every person named in 245$c beyond the 100 main entry \(or every named person, if entry is under title\)\.

### Exceptions and special cases

- If 245$c uses '\[et al\.\]' to truncate a long list, additional 700 fields may still be added for the omitted names if their identity is known and access is wanted\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Skipping 700 added entries for translators/illustrators/editors named in 245$c — every named contributor should normally be independently retrievable\.

## 710 — Added Entry — Corporate Name

Access point for a corporate body associated with the work that does NOT meet the 21\.1B main\-entry test — most commonly the publisher, sponsoring body, or issuing agency\.

*Source: AACR2 21\.30E  |  ISBD —  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 710*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

710

$a

Corporate name

Natural word order, no comma\.

World Health Organization

710

$e

Relator term

publisher, issuing body, sponsoring body\.

issuing body

Required vs\. optional: Given whenever a corporate body is significantly associated with the work but is not the main entry\.

## 711 — Added Entry — Meeting Name

Access point for a meeting/conference associated with the work that is not the 111 main entry\.

*Source: AACR2 21\.30F  |  ISBD —  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 711*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

711

$a

Meeting name

Natural word order\.

International Conference on AI

711

$d

Date

Numeric year of the meeting\.

2024

Required vs\. optional: Given whenever a named meeting is associated with the work but is not the main entry\.

## 800 — Series Added Entry — Personal Name

Provides an access point for the AUTHOR OF THE SERIES \(as distinct from the author of the individual work\), when the series itself has a named personal author/editor\.

*Source: AACR2 21\.30L; 1\.6  |  ISBD Area 6 \(in conjunction with 490\)  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 800*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

800

$a

Personal name \(series author\)

Surname, First name\.

Sharma, Anita

800

$t

Title of the series

Uniform title of the series, if used\.

Hamlyn lectures

Required vs\. optional: Given only where the series itself is attributed to a named person and the record uses 490/800 \(rather than a bare 440\) for series control\.

## 856 — Electronic Location and Access

Records a URL/URI giving electronic access to the item or to supplementary material about it\.

*Source: AACR2 — \(introduced with electronic resources; addressed in the ISBD 2021 Update for electronic resource description\)  |  ISBD Area 4 \(electronic resources\); 2021 Update guidance on online resource access  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 856*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

856

$3

Materials specified

Describes what the link leads to \(e\.g\. Publisher's description, Table of contents\)\.

Publisher's description

856

$u

Uniform Resource Identifier

Full, working URL\.

https://www\.loc\.gov/catdir/enhancements/fy0665/2006297074\-d\.html

Required vs\. optional: $u is required whenever an electronic link is recorded; $3 recommended so users know what the link contains before clicking\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Adding a URL without $3, leaving users unsure whether the link is the full text, a preview, or a publisher's blurb\.
- Not verifying the URL resolves before saving the record\.

## 942 — Added Elements \(KOHA local field\)

KOHA\-specific field controlling item type / record\-level defaults used for circulation, not an AACR2/ISBD/MARC\-standard bibliographic element\.

*Source: AACR2 — \(local system field, not AACR2\)  |  ISBD — \(outside ISBD\)  |  MARC 21 Bibliographic Format, field 942*

__Tag__

__Sub\-field__

__Field Name__

__Cataloguing Rule \(what to enter\)__

__Example__

942

$c

Item type

Selected from KOHA's drop\-down list — Book, Reference, Stack, Bare Act, etc\.

Book

Required vs\. optional: Required by KOHA to correctly apply circulation rules to the item\.

### Common mistakes to avoid

- Leaving the item type at the system default instead of selecting the correct value for reference/non\-circulating material\.

# 5\. Choice and Form of Main/Added Entry \(AACR2 Chapter 21\)

This governs WHICH heading becomes the 1XX main entry versus a 7XX added entry — a decision made independently of, and prior to, filling in 245$c\.
